extracted.intended_audience: early-career assistant professors in biomedical/chemistry at U.S. institutions; institutional nominators and prospective Searle Scholars applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Selection criteria and process for the Searle Scholars Program, an early-career fellowship awarding ~$300K over 3 years to assistant professors pursuing high-risk, high-reward biomedical/chemistry research. Describes eligibility thresholds, evaluation stages, explicit programmatic biases, and the implicit qualities reviewers seek in applicants and proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary criterion: long-term potential for innovative, high-impact research
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential of applicants to make innovative and high-impact contributions to research over an extended period of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is operationalized through assessment of both the proposal and the applicant (their record and vision). It is the single primary criterion guiding selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic bias: support for high-risk, high-reward research
rubrics_metrics.description: The program explicitly supports 'high risk, high reward' research — projects that are non-incremental and potentially transformative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searle explicitly favors risk-taking research directions, which differentiates it from funders that favor incremental work. Proposals that embrace substantial uncertainty but promise large payoff are viewed positively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility (threshold requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must meet all stated eligibility thresholds to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: independent investigator at assistant professor level; first tenure-track position (or nearest equivalent); appointment must have begun on or after May 1 of two years before competition; U.S. institution required; one nomination per institution (limited submission). These are hard cutoffs — failure to meet them disqualifies an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible research areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must fall within the program's listed scientific domains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible areas include biochemistry, cell biology, genetics, immunology, neuroscience, pharmacology, and related areas in chemistry, medicine, and the biological sciences. Proposals outside these domains are not appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-stage evaluation process (initial reduction then SAB review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection is conducted in two stages: an initial review reduces the pool to ~40 finalists, followed by a two-day Scientific Advisory Board (SAB) meeting to select ~15 awardees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical numbers: ~150–200 applications received, reduced to ~40 finalists, with ~15 awards (~10% acceptance). The SAB is composed of distinguished scientists, many former Searle Scholars, and conducts in-person, holistic evaluation over two days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (non-incremental research direction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should be non-incremental and present novel approaches or ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovation is explicitly prized; proposals that extend current work only incrementally are less competitive. Applicants should emphasize novel hypotheses, techniques, or conceptual frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk tolerance (acceptance of projects that might fail interestingly)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals that carry substantial risk — including the possibility of failure — are acceptable and can be advantageous if the potential payoff is large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searle's explicit bias toward high risk/high reward means reviewers expect and will not penalize justified uncertainty. Framing risky aspects as deliberate, informative experiments (e.g., 'might fail interestingly') is beneficial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent vision distinct from prior mentors
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant should demonstrate an independent scientific vision distinct from their PhD/postdoc training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for projects and a research agenda that show intellectual independence rather than extensions of a mentor's program. Emphasize novel directions, unique hypotheses, and the applicant's leadership of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career trajectory promise
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence that the applicant has the potential for a strong, sustained research career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors consider signs of future impact: early accomplishments, leadership, trajectory of independence, and how the proposed work positions the applicant for a notable career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the science (rigor and scientific merit)
rubrics_metrics.description: The scientific quality and rigor of the proposed research are evaluated at the proposal level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even with tolerance for risk, proposals must present sound scientific rationale, coherent aims, and a convincing plan. Clarity of hypothesis and feasible experimental approaches (where appropriate) strengthen competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional environment and support
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant's institutional setting must be appropriate to support the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider whether the host institution provides the resources, facilities, and mentorship environment necessary for success. Evidence of institutional commitment or suitability is beneficial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award structure and allowable use
rubrics_metrics.description: $300,000 total over 3 years, unrestricted use within the lab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds are provided as an unrestricted award (~$100K/year) with no detailed accounting requirements; applicants can propose uses aligned with advancing their independent research program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation emphasis: holistic, qualitative judgment over quantitative preliminaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Searle's two-stage, in-person SAB review allows holistic qualitative judgments that can override narrow, quantitative rubric metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication for applicants: prioritize communicating vision, high-impact potential, and independence rather than overloading the proposal with extensive preliminary data or rigid feasibility metrics. The SAB format favors narrative and potential over checkbox-style evidence.
